The block is the product's entry point for coding agents in user repositories. Ratified 2026-08-24, 158 tokens under o200k_base. Ratified text:

## Provenance

Requirements live in a Provenance graph. Plan changes with the graph and update
it in the same change.

- Plan: `provenance prime --quiet`
- New obligation: `provenance rules create --scope default --id rule_<slug> --requirement-id <req> --statement "<testable clause>"`
- Annotate implementation with `rule`, tests with `verifies`. Annotations move
  with code.
- To change a Requirement, Rule, or past decision, create a Proposal. A human decides each
  Proposal.
- Pre-commit: `provenance check --quiet` and
  `provenance coverage scan --path . --scope default --validate-rules`.
  Commit graph updates with the code.

description: Four record kinds, source, requirement, resolution, and rule, joined by typed edges: a source references the requirements it motivates and needs a resolution; a resolution resolves the requirement and produces rules. 'provenance traceability <rule-id>' walks the chain back from any rule. A requirement without a source is surfaced as a gap, not rejected.

The requirement tree provides hierarchy; Provenance derives structural context from the rule's graph chain. description: Compressed from the 27 run-machinery rules among the 38 imported PROV-IDEATE records (the other eleven: six were tests written as rules, five superseded by bound rules by shipped rules) written for the Statesman cloud ideation runner and never built. Their themes, kept so nothing is lost silently: a run targets one artifact and posts participant comments plus a synthesis to that artifact's thread; a stable run id ties the work item, participant executions, comments, synthesis, proposal cards, retries and promotions together; an explicit status lifecycle (queued, running, synthesizing, succeeded, partial, failed_retryable, failed_terminal, cancelled) never reports a run with a failed participant as succeeded; an input snapshot records target, sources, graph scope, profile and prompt versions, models and budgets; maximums for participants, rounds, model calls, tokens, wall-clock and generated bytes are enforced before execution and fail the run visibly; cancellation and deadlines stop new work, keep finished output and mark unfinished slots; participant writes are keyed deterministically so a retried slot updates one logical output instead of duplicating it; failures carry the failed step, retry state and diagnostics, and unsafe output is recorded as a sanitized marker rather than posted; participant comments carry stance, strongest finding, evidence references, risks, objections, suggested changes, uncertainty and open questions, and a challenge names the comment it challenges; synthesis preserves consensus, contested claims, minority objections, evidence gaps and open questions instead of collapsing them, stays short enough to read as a brief, and emits typed proposal cards recording their origin comments, claims, evidence level, dissent, confidence and target, with duplicates merged or marked; a promoted artifact links back to the run, synthesis, origin comments, proposal card and approval event; the thread shows outcomes before transcripts, keeps raw output as secondary, and shows the persona label apart from the executing identity; a run reads and writes only inside its target's scope and respects source access and redaction. What shipped instead is the proposal, assertion and disposition model in the ideation records; none of the run machinery above exists.
